correctness.rationale: For each integer \(m\ge2\), the cited deterministic pure-state stabilizer monotonicity of the stabilizer Rényi entropy is exactly equivalent, because \(1-m<0\), to \(P_m(\psi)\le P_m(\phi)\). Nonnegative summation preserves this order, and the logarithmic normalization reverses no inequality. Absolute convergence follows from \(0<P_m\le1\). Faithfulness is proved from \(P_1=1\): equality at any positively weighted order \(m\ge2\) forces every Pauli expectation to have modulus zero or one, hence exactly \(2^n\) unit-modulus commuting Pauli stabilizers. The hyperbolic-cosine series reproduces the cited core partition function term by term and its dimension and Boltzmann factors cancel in the stabilizer-work ratio.
risks: The conclusion depends on the deterministic pure-state protocol notion exactly as defined in the cited stabilizer-entropy theorem; stronger free-operation classes are not inferred.

value.rationale: The theorem turns a collection of integer-order monotones into an infinite coefficient cone of faithful magic monotones and directly covers the finite-temperature stabilizer work used in a recent one-shot conversion argument. This is a reusable structural statement rather than a parameter substitution: it identifies the exact positivity mechanism—coefficientwise order of all normalized Pauli moments—and makes clear which extensions do and do not follow.
risks: The proof is short once the integer-order theorem is known, and it does not extend to strong measurement monotonicity; its value rests on the general closure principle and the load-bearing recent application rather than technical length.
